teams.heading: Jake White calls on Ireland to travel to Pacific Islands
teams.body: Speaking at the Fitzpatrick Castle Hotel, where Fiji have been based this week, the 62-year-old made clear where he would like the next meeting played: "There'd be nothing greater than for Fiji to host Ireland in Suva." It came ahead of Saturday's Nations Championship clash in Dublin, which Fiji went into bottom of the Southern Hemisphere table, winless from four matches. White, who started the job last month, is focused on making Fiji a more consistent force before next year's World Cup in Australia.

lead.why: It is the only genuinely new Fiji item left on the shortlist once the White relocation and Higgins stories, both already reported, are set aside.

teams.heading: England's seven-try win over Australia at Twickenham eases pressure on Borthwick
teams.body: Australia were beaten 45-22 at Allianz Stadium Twickenham, and the BBC framed the result as emphatic on-pitch backing for head coach Steve Borthwick. It was England's Round 4 win in the Nations Championship, and they scored seven tries against what the BBC described as a listless Australia side. Henry Pollock scored two tries after replacing the injured Immanuel Feyi-Waboso at the break, switching to the wing.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus' front-row swap before France not forbidden by Nations Championship rules
teams.body: South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus swapped his starting and replacement front rows shortly before the match, and Rugbyrama reports the move was not forbidden by the Nations Championship regulations. Under the rules of the game, teams must name 15 starters and eight replacements 48 hours before the match, with late changes allowed only for injury. Rugbyrama says a match commissioner at the World Cup or Six Nations would not have validated such a change, but this competition's rulebook allows changes to the starting XV in theory possible.

lead.why: A new item on the pre-match front-row switch, which is a different story from the match reports already run.

teams.heading: Ryan Baird recalls playing on against South Africa with a broken leg
teams.body: The bang Baird took against South Africa in Dublin last November felt like a dead leg, so he played on. Beirne, he says, told him to come off if he could not run, and an X-ray showed the leg was broken. Baird calls the year that followed “soul-sapping”, but says he came back for two URC games and a Heineken Cup quarter-final.

teams.heading: Andrea Di Giandomenico named Italy U20 side to face France in Parma
teams.body: Italy U20 faced France U20 on Friday in the first test of their 2026-27 season, a side blending returning players with newcomers. The 28-man squad gathered at the Cittadella del Rugby in Parma from Monday 9 November, with the aim of bringing younger players into the group. The last meeting, the U20 Six Nations in Lille in February, ended 32-17 to France, with Enoch Opoku Gyamfi shown a 20-minute red card.

teams.heading: Tuipulotu says Scotland are set on bouncing back from All Blacks defeat
teams.body: Sione Tuipulotu, the Australia-born captain, says Scotland have confronted the footage of the 21-43 defeat to New Zealand and are determined to respond. "That performance wasn't good enough. We know that and we want to put that right," he said. He says he will always have "that little bit of fire" when he plays Australia, whom he expects to arrive "wounded" after losing to England at Twickenham.

teams.heading: Wales end 73-year All Blacks wait with 35-28 Principality win
teams.body: Saturday's Nations Championship win over New Zealand at the Principality Stadium ended a run of 34 straight defeats to the All Blacks, with the last Welsh victory coming in 1953. Wales scored a record five tries, but the defining feature was a defensive effort that held New Zealand over the line five times and produced 341 tackles. Former captain Sam Warburton told ITV it was "one of the greatest wins in Wales' history."

teams.heading: Contepomi shuffles XV, moving Delguy to fullback for Genoa win
teams.body: Juan Cruz Mallía's sprained knee, suffered against Ireland, forced Felipe Contepomi into a five-change reshuffle for Genoa. Bautista Delguy moved to fullback, Isgró started on the wing and Simón Benítez Cruz came in at scrum-half, while Matera shifted to No. 8 with Scelzo and Moro in the back row. Bautista Bernasconi started at hooker in place of the unavailable Julián Montoya, with Facundo Bosch on the bench. Argentina won 19-14.

teams.heading: Warner Dearns recalls reluctant move from New Zealand to Japan at 14
teams.body: Dearns admits he did not want to move: "I said I didn't want to go," he recalls of the switch from New Zealand's North Island to a city outside Tokyo, when his father took a job at NEC Green Rockets. At Kashiwa Senior High School he switched from basketball to rugby. He qualified on residency grounds and debuted for Japan in November 2021 at 19. This season, on sabbatical, he helped the Hurricanes win their first Super Rugby title in a decade.

lead.why: It is the freshest Japan-specific item in the pack that is not already in a published edition, and it is a player story a fan would forward.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie's All Blacks beaten 35-28 by Wales at Principality Stadium
teams.body: New Zealand's 34-match winning run over Wales ended on Saturday, when Steve Tandy's side scored five tries to win 35-28. Wales led by 14 points three times, with Tomos Williams, Dewi Lake and Archie Griffin among their try-scorers, and James Botham was named man of the match. Cortez Ratima, Wallace Sititi and Fehi Fineanganofo crossed for New Zealand, who clawed back to 21-21 before the Welsh defence repelled wave after wave of black jerseys. Dave Rennie had made eight changes from the side that beat Scotland.

teams.heading: Ruan Nortjé rejects cards as excuse for Springboks' Paris defeat to France
teams.body: Lock Ruan Nortjé has declined to use the yellow card and 20-minute red his side had to answer for as an excuse for Friday's 19-21 loss to France. Speaking to Planet Rugby, he noted that France also played 30 minutes a man down. "We can't put the blame on that at all," he said, calling France deserving winners. The bigger worry is the Nations Championship, where defeat means South Africa no longer control their route to the final and must rely on other results, with Ireland up next.

lead.why: It is the strongest fresh item on the shortlist, a new player response to the Paris defeat, rather than a rehash of the referee or front-row stories already run.
